items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I saw Milt yesterday at the shoot. 86. I told him I said, “did you hear the song that Mr. Clark Terry sang to me?”

ctx.x: I hope it’s not like what I’ve heard about Milt Hinton’s basement or something you know.
I saw Milt yesterday at the shoot. 86. I told him I said, “did you hear the song that Mr. Clark Terry sang to me?” He says, “no, which one?” [sings] “Who is Milton Hinton’s lady? Mona.” He fell down.
What a wonderful — What’s in the immediate future for you? European tour?

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Big band, yeah with… Max Roach starts it with his tempo and John Henry puts words to Frank Foster‟s [musical sounds], Think you can make it, go to the wicket, buy you a ticket and go, New York, New York [unintelligible].

ctx.x: New York, New York, right. That was a great… it was a big band, right.

Big band, yeah with… Max Roach starts it with his tempo and John Henry puts words to Frank Foster‟s [musical sounds], Think you can make it, go to the wicket, buy you a ticket and go, New York, New York [unintelligible]. So great you had a neighbor”. Then the band comes in [musical sounds]. Great record, great. Something like… it was a very good jazz record. Cannonball is on that… not Cannonball, Coltrane with Bill Evans is on that record and the trumpets read like Who‟s Who. [Unintelligible] all those great guys.
Well tell me, you recorded with a lot of groups and earlier you alluded to the fact that one of the things that you always wanted to do was to put bass players together…
